summary.text: 睡 is analyzed as a phonosemantic compound: 目 contributes an eye-related meaning and 垂 supplies a sound cue. Its traditional gloss is “sleep while sitting”; the character means “sleep” or “doze” in current use.

formation.text: Phonosemantic: the traditional analysis combines 目 for an eye-related meaning with 垂 as the phonetic element. The Shuowen gloss is “sleep while sitting.”

components.text: 目 means “eye” and contributes an eye-related semantic association in 睡; it does not depict a whole sleeping scene.
垂 is identified as the sound element. The Baxter–Sagart comparison is close, with an added *-s suffix in 睡; the comparison supports but does not by itself prove this role.

sound.text: Baxter–Sagart reconstructs 垂 as *[d]o[j] and 睡 as *[d]o[j]-s, a close same-system comparison with an added suffix in 睡.
The locally recorded Mandarin readings are chuí for 垂 and shuì for 睡. This modern pair is a reading comparison, not evidence by itself for their historical phonetic relationship.

history.text: The Shuowen account analyzes 睡 as made from 目 and 垂. A later commentary explains the eye element through drooping eyelids; this is an interpretation of the graph, not proof of its earliest construction.
No verified early inscription or physical image is available here to trace 睡’s graphic evolution. A modern redrawing in seal-script style does not document an ancient artifact.

uncertainties.text: The earliest physical attestation and detailed graphic evolution of 睡 remain unresolved. The cited transmitted texts do not establish manuscript dates or a chronology from sleeping while seated to broader sleep and lying down.
The reconstructed sound comparison supports the phonetic analysis but does not prove it by itself. The Mandarin readings come from local data; the direct Unihan character pages could not be verified.

senses.period: dating unresolved; gloss in the transmitted Shuowen account
senses.text: The Shuowen gloss is “sleep while sitting.” It provides an early lexical framing, but does not establish manuscript dates or that this was the word’s original meaning.

senses.period: attested in transmitted classical examples; dating unresolved
senses.text: Transmitted text examples use 睡 for sleeping or dozing. The evidence does not establish when this broader use arose relative to the sitting-sleep gloss.

senses.period: Qing example recorded; exact chronology unresolved
senses.text: A later example is glossed “lie down.” The evidence does not establish a semantic path from sleeping to lying down.

limitations.text: The evidence records distinct historical and current uses but does not establish a chronological chain among sleeping while seated, broader sleep, and lying down; no semantic-development links are asserted.

overview.text: 睡 combines 目, “eye,” with 垂 as a sound element. Its traditional gloss is “sleep while sitting”; today it means “sleep” or “doze.”

components.text: 目 links 睡 to the eyes, the body part associated with sleep.
垂 supplies a sound cue; the historical reconstructions are close, with an added suffix in 睡.

relationships.text: Within 睡, 目 contributes the eye-related semantic association in the traditional analysis.

The traditional analysis assigns 垂 a sound role. Baxter–Sagart reconstructs 垂 as *[d]o[j] and 睡 as *[d]o[j]-s, a close same-system comparison with an added suffix in 睡; this supports but does not independently prove the role.
